subject: physiology
title: Salivary Secretion, Gastric Acid, and the Parietal Cell

steps.tx: Normal adults produce approximately one to one point five litres of saliva daily, secreted by paired parotid, submandibular, and sublingual glands. Secretion begins in acini as an isotonic plasma-like primary fluid, but extensive ductile modification produces a final **hypotonic salivary secretion** rich in bicarbonate and potassium.
steps.say: Salivary glands secrete an isotonic primary fluid that ducts modify into hypotonic saliva rich in bicarbonate and potassium.

left.title: Acino-Tubular Primary Secretion
points: Secreted by serous and mucous acinar cells
Sodium and chloride concentrations resemble plasma

right.title: Ductal Reabsorption and Secretion
points: Ductal epithelium actively reabsorbs Na+ and Cl-
Ducts actively secrete K+ and HCO3-
Ductal epithelium is strictly impermeable to water
Final saliva becomes distinctly hypotonic (~100 mOsm/kg)

steps.tx: Because salivary ductal epithelium is completely impermeable to water, active reabsorption of sodium and chloride without water withdrawal renders saliva increasingly hypotonic at resting low flow rates. When salivation is stimulated, transit through ducts accelerates, causing salivary sodium and bicarbonate concentrations to rise toward **plasma electrolyte levels**.
steps.say: At high flow rates, ducts have less time to reabsorb sodium and chloride, making saliva less hypotonic.

steps.tx: Unlike other digestive secretions governed predominantly by peptide hormones, salivary secretion is regulated exclusively by autonomic neural reflexes. While parasympathetic stimulation via acetylcholine generates profuse, watery saliva rich in enzymes, sympathetic stimulation via noradrenaline elicits **viscous mucous salivation** with high mucin content.
steps.say: Salivation is controlled purely by autonomic nerves: parasympathetics trigger watery saliva, and sympathetics cause thick mucous secretion.

left.title: Parasympathetic Control (Dominant)
points: Cranial nerves VII (chorda tympani) and IX (glossopharyngeal)
Releases acetylcholine acting on M3 muscarinic receptors
Yields profuse, watery saliva with high enzyme content

right.title: Sympathetic Control
points: Preganglionic T1-T3 fibers synapsing in superior cervical ganglion
Releases noradrenaline acting on beta-adrenergic receptors
Yields small volume of thick, viscous, mucin-rich saliva

steps.tx: In the gastric mucosa, oxyntic glands contain specialized acid-secreting **gastric parietal cells**, located predominantly in the fundus and body of the stomach. Under maximal stimulation, parietal cells secrete concentrated hydrochloric acid at a concentration of one hundred fifty millimoles per litre, creating a luminal pH under zero point eight.
steps.say: Gastric parietal cells in the fundus and body secrete hydrochloric acid, driving stomach pH down to near one.

vis.alt: Gastric parietal cell ultrastructure and canalicular network
vis.caption: Parietal cell apical canaliculi, tubulovesicular transformation, and proton pump dynamics.

steps.tx: Active proton transport against an immense million-fold concentration gradient is driven by the apical **gastric proton pump**, or hydrogen-potassium ATPase. This electro-neutral P-type ATPase hydrolyzes adenosine triphosphate to pump hydrogen ions into the gastric lumen in exchange for potassium ions.
steps.say: The hydrogen-potassium ATPase proton pump uses ATP to extrude hydrogen ions against a million-fold gradient.

nodes.label: Intracellular Carbonic Anhydrase-II Hydrates CO2 to Carbonic Acid (H2CO3)
Dissociation Generates Free Protons (H+) and Bicarbonate Ions (HCO3-)
Apical H+/K+-ATPase Pumps H+ into Gastric Lumen in Exchange for K+
Apical Chloride Channels Extrude Cl-, Forming Luminal Concentrated HCl

steps.tx: As hydrogen ions are extruded into the gastric lumen, equimolar amounts of intracellular bicarbonate are exported into the peritubular bloodstream via basolateral anion exchanger 1. This surge of bicarbonate entering gastric venous circulation following a meal produces the transient physiological **postprandial alkaline tide**.
steps.say: Export of bicarbonate into gastric veins during acid production creates the postprandial alkaline tide in blood and urine.

Gastric Venous Blood Bicarbonate Rises (Postprandial Alkaline Tide)
Transient Rise in Systemic Blood pH Elicits Mild Urinary Alkalinization

steps.tx: Parietal cell acid secretion is stimulated by three converging physiological secretagogues: acetylcholine from vagal endings acting on M3 receptors, gastrin from G cells acting on CCK-B receptors, and histamine from enterochromaffin-like cells acting on H2 receptors. Histamine acts via cyclic adenosine monophosphate, providing **potentiation of acid secretion**.
steps.say: Acetylcholine, gastrin, and histamine stimulate parietal cells, synergistically potentiating each other to maximize acid secretion.

steps.tx: Pharmacological inhibition of acid secretion is achieved irreversibly by **proton pump inhibitors** like omeprazole, which accumulate within acidic canaliculi and bind covalently to cysteine residues on the hydrogen-potassium ATPase. They suppress basal and stimulated acid secretion by over ninety percent, treating peptic ulcer disease and reflux.
steps.say: Proton pump inhibitors covalently block hydrogen-potassium ATPases, suppressing acid secretion by over ninety percent.
